messages:
sam: quick q — we're setting up temporary infra role bindings via SCIM for on-call escalations. what's the recommended way to ensure auto-deprovision after X hours? do we rely on Okta, SCIM attributes, or a Redwood scheduled job?

jess: Okta/SCIM doesn't have a built-in expiry lifecycle for group membership. most folks add a custom attribute (e.g. redwood:role_expires) on the user or membership, then run a scheduled worker that patches membership out when expiry passes.

mike: agreed. example SCIM PATCH we use for expiries:
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "Add",
      "path": "meta.extensions.redwood",
      "value": { "role_expires": "2026-05-10T12:00:00Z" }
    }
  ]
}
```
note: the scheduler only reads the extension and removes group membership; we do NOT rely on Okta to auto-remove.

amelia: are we comfortable logging the extension value? that's a timestamp, but could be sensitive if we also log who requested it. need to make sure logs are redacted per the privacy policy.

mike: we log events like `membership_removed` / `membership_created` with user_id (hashed) and group name only. DO NOT log the full Okta user profile or email. example event we send to SIEM: `{ event: "scim.membership_removed", user_hash: "sha256:...", group: "temp-infra" }` (values redacted/hashed).

jess: +1. Also make sure the scheduled job writes an audit record to the internal audit table (not plain logs) with requestor id and approval ticket id. audit table is access-controlled and encrypted at rest.

sam: question on approvals — who signs off on short-lived infra roles (<72h)? is security@ an auto-approve or manual?

amelia: policy: anything >24h needs approval from security and the owning product/team lead. under 24h we allow team lead + 2FA flag. we'll add this to the docs.

sec-bot: compliance-check: remember to enable `log_redaction: true` on the scim-worker config and set `audit_retention_days` per policy.

mike: ops detail: the worker looks for `meta.extensions.redwood.role_expires` and `meta.extensions.redwood.request_id`. when removing it emits to SIEM and also calls the internal approvals API to mark the request closed. code sketch:
```bash
# pseudo
scim-scheduler --scan-interval=10m --redact=true 
```

jess: small security note — avoid storing ISO expiry in plaintext in debugging logs. if someone runs a local debug with `SCIM_DEBUG=true` it must still redact extension values.

sam: got it. i'll draft the PR: 1) add scheduler job, 2) update scim-worker config to redact, 3) doc the approval flow and ticket template. i'll tag everyone for review. :thumbsup:

amelia: please cc security@ and add the approval checklist in the ticket so on-call can follow it.

mike: :eyes: i'll review the PR tomorrow.

sam: thanks all — opening ticket now: https://redwood.internal/requests/REQ-1248
